Here is a focused 1-week deload designed to maintain movement patterns, reduce cumulative fatigue, and prepare the client for the upcoming intensification block. It uses the same primary exercises as a typical full-gym hypertrophy program, but with reduced volume and lower intensity (RPE ~5–6). Total weekly demand is significantly lower while preserving technique and work capacity.

Client snapshot (for reference)
- Age: 26, male
- Training history: Advanced, just completed 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy
- Current block: High-volume hypertrophy (18 working sets per session, RPE ~8.5 on compounds)
- Goal of deload: Restore readiness, CNS recovery, maintain movement patterns, and set up for the next intensification block

Deload structure overview
- Duration: 7 days
- Frequency: 4 sessions (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) or adjust to client schedule
- Intensity: RPE ~5–6 on main sets
- Volume: Approximately 40–60% of recent training volume; aims to preserve technique, not achieve new adaptations
- Rest periods: 60–90 seconds for accessory lifts; 2–3 minutes for main lifts if needed
- Focus: Technique mastery, mobility work, breathing, injury prevention, and passive/active recovery

Proposed weekly schedule (example)
- Day 1: Push (bench/overhead variations with reduced volume)
- Day 2: Pull (row/lat pull variations with reduced volume)
- Day 3: Rest or light mobility
- Day 4: Legs (squat/hinge pattern with reduced volume)
- Day 5: Tempo/assistant work and mobility
- Day 6: Optional light total-body work or cardio/conditioning
- Day 7: Rest

Detailed deload plan by session

Session A – Push (Upper Body Push emphasis)
Main lifts (keep same exercises as in normal hypertrophy program, but reduced volume and intensity)
- Bench Press or Dumbbell Bench (flat or incline): 3 sets x 4–6 reps, RPE 5–6
- Overhead Press (barbell or dumbbell): 2 sets x 6–8 reps, RPE 5–6
Accessory and mobility:
- Dips or Ring DMD (or push-ups if needed): 2 sets x 8–10 reps, easy pace
- Chest fly variation (cable or dumbbell): 2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Lateral raises: 2 sets x 12–15 reps
- Triceps pushdown or skullcrushers: 2 sets x 12–15 reps
Core:
- Pallof press or anti-rotation hold: 2 sets x 20–30 seconds

Notes:
- Keep bench press around 60–70% of 1RM if known; otherwise stay in RPE 5–6 range.
- Emphasize technique, slower eccentric where appropriate.

Session B – Pull (Upper Body Pull emphasis)
Main lifts:
- Barbell or Dumbbell Row: 3 sets x 5–7 reps, RPE 5–6
- Lat Pulldown or Pull-ups (assisted if needed): 2–3 sets x 6–8 reps, RPE 5–6
Accessory:
- Seated Cable Row or T-bar row: 2 sets x 8–10 reps
- Face pulls: 2 sets x 12–15 reps
- Dumbbell Curls or Spider Curls: 2 sets x 10–12 reps
Mobility/Shoulder health:
- Band dislocations or wall slides: 2 sets x 12–15 reps
Core:
- Plank variations: 2 x 30–45 seconds

Session C – Legs (Quadriceps/Hamstrings emphasis)
Main lifts:
- Back Squat or Front Squat: 3 sets x 4–6 reps, RPE 5–6
- Romanian Deadlift or Stiff-Legged Deadlift: 2 sets x 6–8 reps, RPE 5–6
Accessory:
- Leg Extension (light): 2 sets x 8–12 reps
- Leg Curl (lying or seated): 2 sets x 8–12 reps
- Calf Raise: 2 sets x 12–15 reps
Core/Mobility:
- Hip hinge drills or posterior chain activation: 2 sets x 10–12 reps
Foam roll and mobility work post-session

Session D – Tempo/Light Total Body + Mobility
Main focus: technique, tempo work, and mobility
- Tempo Squat or Leg Press: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps at controlled tempo (e.g., 3-0-2-0) with light load
- Tempo Bench or Push-Ups: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps with controlled tempo
- Seated Row or Cable Row: 2 sets x 10–12 reps
- Lat Pulldown or assisted pull-ups: 2 sets x 8–10 reps
- Core: Pallof press or dead bug: 3 sets x 10–12 reps
Mobility:
- Hip mobility routine, chest openers, thoracic spine mobility
Breathing and recovery:
- 5–10 minutes dedicated to diaphragmatic breathing, meditation or light mobility work

Optional Day 6 (active recovery or light conditioning)
- Low-intensity cardio: 20–30 minutes at conversational pace (bike, row, brisk walk)
- Full-body mobility and light activation: 15–20 minutes
- Optional light skill work (yoga flow, mobility sequence)

Volume and intensity targets
- Volume: Aim for roughly 40–60% of the client’s previous week’s training volume. If the client did 18 working sets in a session previously, target around 7–10 working sets for the deload main lifts, plus accessory sets totaling around 14–18 sets for the session, spread across push, pull, and legs days.
- Intensity: Keep RPE 5–6 for the main lifts. If using autoregulation, ensure loads don’t push RPE beyond 6.
- Rest periods: 60–90 seconds for accessories; 2–3 minutes for main lifts if needed to maintain form with lighter loads.

Recovery components
- Sleep: Target 7–9 hours per night; encourage consistent sleep/wake times.
- Nutrition: Maintain protein intake around 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; moderate carbohydrate intake to support training and recovery; hydration: 3–4 L/day depending on body size and sweat rate.
- Hydration and electrolytes: Consider electrolytes on heavier days, even during deload (especially if training volume is reduced, to maintain performance and recovery).
- Mobility and soft tissue: 10–15 minutes of mobility work daily; light myofascial release if available (foam roller, lacrosse ball) focused on T-spine, hips, and ankles.
- Stress management: 5–10 minutes of breathing or mindfulness daily; consider light walking or mobility sessions on rest days.

Supportive notes for you as the trainer
- Communicate deload intent to the client: emphasize recovery, technique work, and readiness for the next phase.
- Use simple progressions: if the client feels fresh mid-deload, you can add a small set or two on a single exercise, but avoid raising overall volume back toward prior levels.
- Monitor for signs of insufficient recovery: persistent fatigue, irritability, poor sleep. If present, adjust next week’s intensification plan accordingly.
- Optional: incorporate one extra mobility session mid-week focusing on hip flexors, hamstrings, thoracic spine, and shoulder girdle.

Transition considerations
- At the end of the deload week, evaluate readiness for the intensification block. Plan a re-test or a lowest-load estimate (progressively increase volume and intensity from deload gradually) to ensure the client isn’t under-recovered or overreaching.
- If you have the exact 1RM forecasts or weekly reps and volumes from the prior block, you can tailor the deload to be slightly heavier/lighter; the above plan is a safe, general deload framework.

If you’d like, share the client’s exact lifts, previous weekly set/rep counts, and any known 1RM estimates, and I’ll tailor the deload with precise set/rep prescriptions for each exercise and a week-by-week readiness check.

From your initial brief, you stated: “Just finished 4 weeks of high-volume hypertrophy — 18 working sets/session, RPE 8.5 across compounds.” That indicates the last-week volume target for the client’s main sessions was 18 working sets per session (not counting warm-ups or optional accessories). However, you asked to base the deload on last week’s exact volume per session, including all components.

Clarifying assumption for precision:
- If “18 working sets” refers to all sets that contribute to hypertrophy (main compounds plus any primary accessories counted as working sets), then we’ll use 18 as the target main-working-set count per session for last week.
- If those 18 sets were strictly main compound lifts (e.g., bench, squat, row, etc.) with little to no accessory sets counted, then the total weekly per-session volume (including synergistic accessory work) would be higher. Since you described 18 working sets “across compounds” and “RPE 8.5 across compounds,” I’ll treat 18 as total working sets per session across all exercises in that hypertrophy block, with a typical distribution across push, pull, legs.

Deload target parameters (based on last week’s 18 working sets per session)
- Target deload main-session working sets: 40–60% of last week’s 18 sets
  - Range: 7–11 sets per session
  - For balance across movements, aim for 9–10 total working sets per deload session (main and accessories combined)
- Session structure approximation (4 deload sessions planned across the week)
  - Session A (Push): 9–10 working sets
  - Session B (Pull): 9–10 working sets
  - Session C (Legs): 9–10 working sets
  - Session D (Tempo/Light Total Body): 8–9 working sets
- Intensity targets: Main lifts at RPE 5–6
- Rest: 60–90 seconds for accessories, 2–3 minutes for main lifts if needed

Concrete, per-session prescriptions (assuming 9–10 total working sets per session)
Session A – Push (total 9–10 working sets)
- Bench Press or Dumbbell Bench: 3 sets x 4–6 reps (RPE 5–6) = 3 sets
- Overhead Press: 2 sets x 6–8 reps (RPE 5–6) = 2 sets
- Dips or Push-ups: 2 sets x 8–10 reps (easy pace) = 2 sets
- Chest Fly variation: 1 set x 10–12 reps = 1 set
- Lateral Raises: 1 set x 12–15 reps = 1 set
- Triceps pushdown or skullcrushers: 0–1 set x 12–15 reps (optional) = 0–1 set
Total: approx 9–10 sets

Session B – Pull (total 9–10 working sets)
- Barbell/Dumbbell Row: 3 sets x 5–7 reps (RPE 5–6) = 3 sets
- Lat Pulldown or Pull-ups: 2 sets x 6–8 reps (RPE 5–6) = 2 sets
- Seated Cable Row or T-Bar Row: 2 sets x 8–10 reps = 2 sets
- Face Pulls: 1–2 sets x 12–15 reps = 1–2 sets
- DB Curls or Spider Curls: 1 set x 10–12 reps = 1 set
Total: approx 9–10 sets

Session C – Legs (total 9–10 working sets)
- Back Squat or Front Squat: 3 sets x 4–6 reps (RPE 5–6) = 3 sets
- Romanian Deadlift or Stiff-Legged Deadlift: 2 sets x 6–8 reps (RPE 5–6) = 2 sets
- Leg Extension: 2 sets x 8–12 reps = 2 sets
- Leg Curl: 1–2 sets x 8–12 reps = 1–2 sets
- Calf Raise: 1 set x 12–15 reps = 1 set
Total: approx 9–10 sets

Session D – Tempo/Light Total Body + Mobility (total 8–9 working sets)
- Tempo Squat or Leg Press: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps at controlled tempo = 2–3 sets
- Tempo Bench or Push-Ups: 2–3 sets x 8–10 reps = 2–3 sets
- Seated Row or Cable Row: 2 sets x 10–12 reps = 2 sets
- Lat Pulldown or Assisted Pull-ups: 1–2 sets x 8–10 reps = 1–2 sets
- Core: Pallof press or dead bug: 2–3 sets x 10–12 reps = 2–3 sets
Total: approx 8–9 sets

Notes
- If you prefer stricter adherence to 9–10 total sets or want to keep day-to-day symmetry, adjust by dropping 1 set from a minor accessory or combining a couple of movements into a single set on one exercise.
- Maintain RPE 5–6 on main lifts; use autoregulation only if the client feels exceptionally fresh, otherwise stay conservative.
- Keep rest 60–90 seconds for most accessories and 2–3 minutes for main lifts.

Recovery and other components (unchanged from prior deload guidance)
- Sleep 7–9 hours nightly
- Protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; moderate carbs; stay hydrated (3–4 L/day, adjust for body size and sweat)
- Daily mobility 10–15 minutes; smart foam rolling
- Breathing and relaxation 5–10 minutes daily
- Monitor fatigue, sleep, and mood; adjust if signs of inadequate recovery appear

If you want, I can tailor the exact set/rep numbers to your client’s exact 1RM estimates and any known training history per lift, or adjust the distribution if you prefer keeping all primary lifts in priority.

Got it. With shoulder crankiness on bench, we’ll preserve chest stimulus while avoiding aggravation. Swap bench variations to maintain pushing demand, emphasize horizontal pressing alternatives that are lower risk to the shoulder, and keep deload volume targets intact.

Guiding changes
- Primary push movement: replace Barbell/Dumbbell Bench with a safer horizontal pressing alternative that reduces shoulder torque and impingement risk.
- Keep overall pushing volume near 9–10 sets per deload session, but reallocate to preserve chest stimulus and deload goals.

Recommended substitutions and per-session updates

Session A – Push (revised)
Main lift (swap bench for safer horizontal press)
- Floor Press or Dumbbell Floor Press: 3 sets x 4–6 reps, RPE 5–6
  - Rationale: benching can aggravate the shoulder; floor press reduces horizontal abduction and removes shoulder lockout strain while still targeting chest and triceps.

Accessory and mobility:

- Floor press reduces shoulder strain while still loading pecs and triceps; ensure a full range of motion without flaring the shoulder.

Session B – Pull (unchanged)
- Keep as previously outlined; shoulder-friendly pulling pattern typically tolerates deload well.

Additional shoulder care and Injury-prevention tips
- Warm-up should include scapular retraction exercises, band pull-aparts, and shoulder external rotation work (0–15 lb bands, 2–3 sets of 12–15 reps) before pressing.
- Prioritize a stable setup: shoulder blades retracted, pack the ribs, and maintain neutral grip on pressing variations.
- Monitor pain: if any movement reproduces sharp pain or pinpoint shoulder pain, reduce ROM or substitute to a more joint-friendly variation (e.g., machine chest press with neutral grip, or incline press with careful angles).

Communication cues for you
- Instruct client to report any twinges or increased symptoms during or after sessions.
- If symptoms persist beyond the deload, consider a longer rehab-focused block (mobility, rotator cuff work, internal/external rotation balance) before reintroducing heavy horizontal pressing.

Great question. For an advanced client in a deload week, you want markers that are informative but don’t erode recovery or push CNS too hard. Focus on low-fatigue, objective measures that give a signal about strength, technique, and readiness without costing you a full training day.

Recommended strength markers that fit a deload week

1) Heavy singles with ample RPE buffer (low volume, safe)
- Rationale: a single or two max-effort attempts in key lifts can flag residual strength without hammering recovery.
- Implementation:
  - Bench press (or the swap floor press): 1–2 sets of 1 rep at a light-reinforced working weight that leaves 2–3 reps in reserve (e.g., if you know a rough 1RM, use ~90–95% of that max for 1RM attempts? Better to stay far from max to reduce CNS load: 1 rep at about 70–85% of estimated 1RM, with 3–5 minutes rest, only if the client is feeling fresh and non-painful.)
  - Back squat: same approach as above, 1 rep at controlled depth and no grinder reps.
- Data to collect: 1RM-ish Single weight and how it felt; bar speed if you have a tempo/velocity app.

2) Technical readiness and movement quality score
- Rationale: deload is perfect for assessing form stability without heavy loading.
- Implementation:
  - Pick 2–3 sets of a controlled submaximal rep pattern in a main movement (e.g., squat depth check, bench-press technique check, or hip hinge pattern).
  - Use a simple 5-point scale for technique: bar path, range of motion, control, bracing, and consistency. Rate each on 0–5, total 0–15 per lift.
- Data to collect: trend across sessions; look for breakdowns or improved control.

3) Velocity-based estimate on a submaximal set
- Rationale: velocity can reflect strength capability without grinding to a grind.
- Implementation:
  - Use a light-to-moderate warm-up set in a main lift (e.g., benches or squats at 60–70% 1RM for 3–5 reps).
  - If you have a velocity app or device, record average velocity (m/s) or velocity loss (e.g., less than 10% drop) vs. baseline.
  - If you don’t have tech, simply compare bar speed visually with your previous cycles and note any obvious speed retention.
- Data to collect: velocity reading or subjective speed note.

4) Submaximal rep-out as an index (low volume)
- Rationale: a brief, controlled rep-out can show endurance and strength without pushing recovery too hard.
- Implementation:
  - Choose a primary lift (e.g., incline press or floor press). Do 3 sets of 3–5 reps at a light load (60–70% 1RM) to technical failure threshold vs. muscular failure. Stop well before CNS fatigue.
- Data to collect: reps completed, RPE of effort, any technique deterioration.

5) Readiness and subjective markers
- Rationale: psychological and physiological readiness is predictive of how you’ll perform in the next block.
- Implementation:
  - Morning readiness survey: sleep quality, perceived energy, muscle soreness scale, mood, appetite.
  - Brief (1–2 minute) movement screen: shoulder/pelvis/ankle mobility check, deep squat pattern, thoracic rotation.
- Data to collect: trend in readiness scores across deload.

6) Optional: grip/upper body strength proxy
- Rationale: quick, non-fatiguing measure that often correlates with overall pressing/pulling strength.
- Implementation:
  - Grip dynamometer or simple handgrip test: max isometric squeeze for 5 seconds on both hands.
- Data to collect: left/right grip strength; compare to baseline if you have it.

Session and day-by-day plan for a deload week with tests
- Day 1 (Push session, with test elements)
  - Warm-up as usual
  - 1–2 heavy-ish singles in floor press (or light floor press) with 3–5 min rest
  - 1 technical readiness set in a bench-like pattern (e.g., push-up with scapular control)
  - Velocity check on a light set if equipment available
  - Record: single rep load and perceived effort; movement quality score
- Day 2 (Pull session)
  - Similar approach for row/lat pull or a light deadlift hinge with 1 rep
  - Technical readiness assessment on a row variation
- Day 3 (Mobility day / cardio day)
  - Keep passive readiness checks: sleep, soreness, mood
- Day 4 (Legs)
  - 1 heavy single in squat variation or goblet if needed
  - Technical readiness check on squat pattern
- Day 5 (Tempo/Light total body)
  - Short velocity check on tempo pattern with light load (optional)
- Day 6–7: Zone 2 cardio and mobility (no testing)

Data handling and interpretation
- Track trends, not isolated numbers. A small weekly change in a single marker is normal; look for consistent direction across markers.
- If you see a drop in strength singles or a decline in movement quality, treat it as CNS/tech fatigue signal and adjust the intensities for the next phase.
- If readiness scores are high and velocity/submax tests hold, you have a positive readiness signal to push into intensification.

Practical tips
- Keep tests low volume, short, and non-fatiguing.
- Avoid any testing that would push into failure or require high CNS load.
- Document all numbers clearly and pair with subjective notes.

If you want, I can tailor exact test reps/loads to your client’s known 1RM estimates and the current deload exercise lineup, and provide a compact scoring sheet you can use each day.

Noted. If he’s feeling great by Wednesday and bored with the low-intensity deload, you can introduce a couple of controlled, conservative push-pull stimuli that raise the intensity slightly without derailing recovery. The goal is to lean into readiness signals while safeguarding the deload’s purpose.

Safety guardrails
- Keep volume at or below the deload target (roughly 40–60% of last week’s volume per session, or about 9–10 total working sets for main sessions).
- Use RPE targets in the 6–7 range on any heavier sets, never pushing toward 8–9 in this week’s deload context.
- Maintain good technique, no grinder reps, and ample rest between sets (3–4 minutes for heavier singles if used, 2–3 minutes for primary lifts).

Proposed schedule adjustment
- Day 3 (Mobility Day): preserve as a light active recovery window, but you can add a short low-fatigue strength re-test or feel-good activation if he’s rating readiness highly. Keep it non-fatiguing.
- Day 4 (Legs): add a light, controlled training block that nudges intensity slightly.
- Day 5 (Tempo/Light Total Body): maintain tempo work, but insert one moderate load set in a main lift with strict form.
- Day 6 & 7: Zone 2 cardio remains optional; monitor fatigue.

Concrete updated prescriptions (Wednesday-Friday push)

Session Wednesday (Re-introduced mild intensity push work)
- Floor Press or Dumbbell Floor Press: 3 sets x 4–6 reps, RPE 6 (slightly harder than deload baseline)
- Overhead Press: 2 sets x 5–7 reps, RPE 6
- Dips or Push-Ups: 2 sets x 8–10 reps, controlled
- Chest Fly variation: 1 set x 10–12 reps
- Lateral Raises: 1 set x 12–15 reps
- Core: Pallof press 2 x 20–30 seconds
Rest: 2–3 minutes between main lifts, 60–90 seconds for accessories

Session Friday (Push-Pull hybrid minimal extra load)
- A light full-body push-pull sequence to spark engagement without overloading deload
  - Bench substitute floor press: 2 sets x 5–6 reps, RPE 6
  - Barbell or Dumbbell Row: 2 sets x 6–8 reps, RPE 6
  - Seated or Cable Row: 1 set x 8–10 reps
  - Face Pulls: 2 sets x 12–15 reps
  - Optional curl or triceps pushdown: 1 set x 10–12 reps
Core: 1 set of dead bug or Pallof press 10–12 reps
Rest: 2 minutes between main lifts; 60–90 seconds for accessories

Monitoring during the adjusted days
- Check fatigue, sleep quality, and joint comfort after each session.
- If any joint pain or sharp discomfort reappears, dial back to the original deload plan immediately.
- If he feels exceptionally recovered, you can tolerate staying at these slightly higher intensities for the day but revert to the stricter deload plan if soreness or fatigue creeps in afterward.

Communication tips
- Frame this as a temporary boost due to high readiness and client interest, with a clear cutoff: if fatigue signs appear, revert to the lower-intensity deload pattern.
- Have him rate readiness again post-session to decide on any further adjustments for the rest of the week and the upcoming intensification block.

Next steps
- If you’d like, I can re-run a precise, day-by-day, 7-day plan with exact sets/reps for Wed and Fri that integrates your bench-substitution, mobility day, Zone 2 cardio, and the new higher-intensity deload days, anchored to the client’s known 1RM estimates and lift choices.

Here’s a concise, at-a-glance summary of the deload week, tying sessions to last week’s volume and intensity.

Last-week baseline (pre-deload)
- Session context: 4 main hypertrophy sessions per week (Push, Pull, Legs, Tempo) with 18 working sets per session (high-volume hypertrophy), RPE ~8.5 on compounds.
- Total volume target for deload (relative): roughly 40–60% of last week’s volume per session.
- Target intensity: main lifts at RPE 5–6; lighter accessories and mobility kept optional.

Deload week structure (4 main sessions + mobility + cardio)
- Session A – Push (revised bench substitute)
  - Main sets: 3x floor press 4–6; 2x overhead press 6–8
  - Accessory: dips/push-ups, chest fly, lateral raises, triceps work
  - Total working sets: about 9–10
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Session B – Pull
  - Main sets: 3x row 5–7; 2x lat pulldown 6–8
  - Accessory: seated row, face pulls, curls
  - Total working sets: about 9–10
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Session C – Legs
  - Main sets: 3x squats 4–6; 2x RDL 6–8
  - Accessory: leg ext, leg curl, calves
  - Total working sets: about 9–10
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Session D – Tempo/Light Total Body
  - Tempo/main: 2–3 sets x 8–10 (squat/leg press; bench/push-ups)
  - Seated row, lat pulldown: 2 sets each
  - Core: Pallof/dead bug
  - Total working sets: about 8–9
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Mobility day
  - 20-minute mobility circuit (thoracic, hips, ankles) with diaphragmatic breathing
  - No heavy loading; non-fatiguing
- Zone 2 cardio
  - 2 sessions x 30 minutes
  - Intensity: Zone 2 (roughly 60–70% maxHR)
  - Purpose: maintain engine and recovery balance without high CNS demand

Volume comparison (deload vs last week)
- Main session volume: Target 7–11 working sets per session (approx. 40–60% of 18 sets). Implemented as ~9–10 sets on each of Sessions A–C, and ~8–9 on Session D.
- Total weekly deload volume across main sessions: roughly 36–40 working sets (down from ~72–72 across 4 sessions in peak week if you counted 18 per session as baseline). The deload keeps 4 days of lifting with substantially reduced load and volume.

Intensity comparison (deload vs last week)
- Main lifts: target RPE 5–6 per set during deload (vs. RPE ~8.5 in the peak week).
- Optional mild intensification days (Wed/Fri tweaks) were kept conservative (RPE 6 for the added sets) and capped to avoid CNS overload.
- Zone 2 cardio and mobility remain recovery-friendly, not replacing lifting intensity but adding benign workload.

Key notes
- The deload preserves movement patterns while ensuring technique and readiness for the next block.
- Shoulder-safe substitutions were used for the push stimulus (floor press instead of bench).
- If fatigue or pain spikes at any point, revert immediately to the stricter deload prescription.

Here’s a concise, at-a-glance summary of the deload week, tying sessions to last week’s volume and intensity.

Last-week baseline (pre-deload)
- Session context: 4 main hypertrophy sessions per week (Push, Pull, Legs, Tempo) with 18 working sets per session (high-volume hypertrophy), RPE ~8.5 on compounds.
- Total volume target for deload (relative): roughly 40–60% of last week’s volume per session.
- Target intensity: main lifts at RPE 5–6; lighter accessories and mobility kept optional.

Deload week structure (4 main sessions + mobility + cardio)
- Session A – Push (revised bench substitute)
  - Main sets: 3x floor press 4–6; 2x overhead press 6–8
  - Accessory: dips/push-ups, chest fly, lateral raises, triceps work
  - Total working sets: about 9–10
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Session B – Pull
  - Main sets: 3x row 5–7; 2x lat pulldown 6–8
  - Accessory: seated row, face pulls, curls
  - Total working sets: about 9–10
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Session C – Legs
  - Main sets: 3x squats 4–6; 2x RDL 6–8
  - Accessory: leg ext, leg curl, calves
  - Total working sets: about 9–10
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Session D – Tempo/Light Total Body
  - Tempo/main: 2–3 sets x 8–10 (squat/leg press; bench/push-ups)
  - Seated row, lat pulldown: 2 sets each
  - Core: Pallof/dead bug
  - Total working sets: about 8–9
  - Intensity: main lifts RPE 5–6
- Mobility day
  - 20-minute mobility circuit (thoracic, hips, ankles) with diaphragmatic breathing
  - No heavy loading; non-fatiguing
- Zone 2 cardio
  - 2 sessions x 30 minutes
  - Intensity: Zone 2 (roughly 60–70% maxHR)
  - Purpose: maintain engine and recovery balance without high CNS demand

Volume comparison (deload vs last week)
- Main session volume: Target 7–11 working sets per session (approx. 40–60% of 18 sets). Implemented as ~9–10 sets on each of Sessions A–C, and ~8–9 on Session D.
- Total weekly deload volume across main sessions: roughly 36–40 working sets (down from ~72–72 across 4 sessions in peak week if you counted 18 per session as baseline). The deload keeps 4 days of lifting with substantially reduced load and volume.

Intensity comparison (deload vs last week)
- Main lifts: target RPE 5–6 per set during deload (vs. RPE ~8.5 in the peak week).
- Optional mild intensification days (Wed/Fri tweaks) were kept conservative (RPE 6 for the added sets) and capped to avoid CNS overload.
- Zone 2 cardio and mobility remain recovery-friendly, not replacing lifting intensity but adding benign workload.

Key notes
- The deload preserves movement patterns while ensuring technique and readiness for the next block.
- Shoulder-safe substitutions were used for the push stimulus (floor press instead of bench).
- If fatigue or pain spikes at any point, revert immediately to the stricter deload prescription.
